abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $\pi\pi N$ effects on top of the two-body $\pi N$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $\pi\Delta(1232)3/2^+$, and $\pi N(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $\pi N$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $\pi\Delta$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.
hook: Including three-body effects, the Roper resonance pole lies near 1346 MeV in the complex energy plane.
summary: The Roper resonance, a heavy excited state of the proton, is hard to pin down in lattice QCD. The authors build an amplitude obeying two- and three-body unitarity, fit it to the SAID P11 partial wave and find the pole at 1346 MeV real part with an imaginary part of about -81 MeV. The result is a fit to existing amplitudes, not a new measurement, and is meant as input for future lattice work.
title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
